narr: A slow moving cold front approached the Ohio Valley from the north on August 30th combined with a weak upper level disturbance. Increasing moisture in response to the advancement of the remnants of Hurricane Ida allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area throughout the day. ||Many of these storms were slow moving and produced heavy downpours that led to multiple instances of flash flooding throughout West Virginia. Multiple roads throughout the state were impassable for a time and high water surrounded residences in a few towns. Significant damage was observed around the town of Hanover in Wyoming County where four bridges and multiple culverts were damaged, preventing access to several residences in the area. During the evening, multiple roads and underpasses were flooded in downtown Huntington.
ev: Gilbert Creek rose out of its banks and led to over a foot of water flowing onto the road at Gilbert Creek Tunnel.
Flooding was observed along Cub Creek near the town of Hanover.

Four roads off of Route 52, including Lower Muzzle Road, Canebreak Road, Garden Gap Road, and North Springs Road, in the town of Hanover were impassable due to small streams flowing out of their banks. Four bridges and one culvert were damaged along North Springs Road, which prevented access to seven residences and led to a few inches of water inside of a church. Two culverts were washed out and one was damaged, impacting four residences along Lower Muzzle Road.
Several private bridges were washed out due to flooding and multiple mudslides occurred near Gilbert Creek.
Flooding was observed along Left Fork Ben Creek near the town of Gilbert.
Flooding was observed along Bull Creek, Mohawk, and Trap Fork around the Panther Area.
Flooding was observed along North Spring Road and Garden Gap Bridge near the town of Hanover.
Flooding was observed along Route 10 and several residences were surrounded by high water in the town of Ranger. Flooding was also observed along 14 Mile Creek to the south of Ranger.

Roads were impassable due to flood waters in Panther, along the Right Hand Fork of Bull Creek, and along Mud Fork. The flooding and resulting saturated grounds caused susceptible trees to fall down and mudslides to occur.
Spring Valley Drive at the intersection with S Jefferson Drive and Route 60 near Camden Park were both impassable due to flash flooding near the Buffalo Creek community.
Licklog Branch Road and Radnor Branch Road were both impassable due to flash flooding near the town of Dunlow.
